stimuli.description: 240 images (120 interior, 120 exterior) of architectural scenes, minimized explicit natural vegetation. Normalized to 4:3 aspect ratio. 20 diverse examples for 6 building types (commercial, educational, government, residential, medical, religious).

limitations: using two-dimensional stimuli may limit the generalizability of these findings to three-dimensional built spaces.

focused here on visual perception of architecture. In doing so, we were unable to make inferences about the contribution of nonvisual sensory features of architectural spaces to perceptions of naturalness, scene similarity, and preference, which we would expect to be substantial.

our dependent variables did not directly test the psychological benefits of naturalistic patterns in buildings. Future studies could use tests of cognitive function, such as working memory tasks, to address more directly whether biophilic features of architecture offer measurable benefits to mental health.
